title: Cologne Christmas markets 2026: dates and a weekend plan
author: Brogan
intro: Cologne's big Christmas markets open on 16 November 2026 and most close on 23 December, with the harbour market running on into January. Here are the dates for each one and a plan for fitting them into a weekend.
seo_title: Cologne Christmas markets 2026: 16 Nov to 23 Dec
seo_description: The cathedral market runs 16 Nov to 23 Dec 2026 and the harbour market 13 Nov to 3 Jan. Dates for every Cologne market and a 2-day weekend plan.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Cathedral market:** 16 Nov to 23 Dec
- **Harbour market:** 13 Nov to 3 Jan
- **Old Town (Heinzels):** from 23 Nov
- **Closed:** Sunday 22 Nov
- **Time needed:** 2 nights

These are the dates the markets and their listings give for 2026, checked in October 2026. Opening hours vary from market to market, so look at each market's own website before you set off.

sections.heading: The markets and their 2026 dates
sections.text:
[Cologne](/destinations/cologne) doesn't have one Christmas market, it has half a dozen big ones, each with its own theme, its own stalls and its own mug. They're close enough together that you can walk between the main ones in an evening.

| Market | Where | 2026 dates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cathedral market | Roncalliplatz, beside the cathedral | 16 Nov to 23 Dec |
| Markt der Engel (angels' market) | Neumarkt | 16 Nov to 23 Dec |
| Nikolausdorf (St Nicholas village) | Rudolfplatz | 16 Nov to 23 Dec |
| Harbour market | By the Chocolate Museum | 13 Nov to 3 Jan |
| Heinzels Wintermärchen | Old Town, Alter Markt and Heumarkt | From 23 Nov into early January |
| Stadtgarten market | Stadtgarten park | Mid-November to 23 Dec |

Watch out: most of the city-centre markets close on Sunday 22 November, a German day of remembrance, and the Old Town market doesn't open until the day after. If you're going that weekend, plan for a quieter Sunday.

The end dates for the Old Town and Stadtgarten markets weren't fixed when we checked, so confirm them on the markets' own sites if you're going late in December.

sections.heading: What each market is like
sections.text:
The **cathedral market** is the one in all the photos: red-roofed stalls under a canopy of lights, a huge Christmas tree in the middle and the twin spires of the cathedral right behind. It's also the busiest, so it's best on a weekday afternoon or late in the evening.

The **angels' market** on Neumarkt is smaller and calmer, with white lights strung through the trees and costumed angels walking between the stalls. It's a good one for crafts and decorations.

- **Old Town market** (Heinzels Wintermärchen) is built around the Heinzelmännchen, little house elves from a Cologne legend, with an ice rink on Heumarkt.
- **Harbour market** by the Chocolate Museum has a maritime theme, with stalls under white sails by the Rhine, and stays open the longest.
- **Nikolausdorf** on Rudolfplatz is the cosiest, by an old city gate.
- **Stadtgarten** is the local favourite, in a park west of the centre, with more food than tourist stalls.

sections.heading: A weekend plan
sections.text:
Two nights is enough to see all the main markets without rushing, and to have a look at the city in daylight too.

| Day | Daytime | Evening |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Friday | Arrive, drop bags near the main station | Cathedral market, then the Old Town market |
| Saturday | Cathedral, the Rhine and the Chocolate Museum | Harbour market, then dinner in a brewery |
| Sunday | Angels' market and Nikolausdorf | Head home |

The cathedral is right next to the main station, so you can be at the first market within five minutes of stepping off the train. The Chocolate Museum is a 15-minute walk along the river from the Old Town, which makes it easy to pair with the harbour market.

Cologne's beer is Kölsch, served in small 0.2-litre glasses. In a traditional brewery the waiter keeps bringing fresh ones until you put a beer mat on top of your glass.

sections.heading: Mugs, food and prices
sections.text:
Every big market sells mulled wine (Glühwein) in its own design of mug, and you pay a deposit on top of the drink. Hand the mug back and you get the deposit back, or keep it as a souvenir, which is what many people do.

- **To eat:** Reibekuchen (potato fritters with apple sauce), bratwurst, roasted chestnuts and gingerbread.
- **To drink:** Glühwein, hot chocolate, and a hot Kölsch-based punch at some stalls.
- **To pay:** most stalls take cards now, but carry some cash for the smaller ones.

As a rough guide, expect a mug of mulled wine plus deposit to cost noticeably more than the drink alone. Prices are on boards at each stall.

sections.heading: Getting there and where to stay
sections.text:
Cologne is one of the easiest German Christmas market cities to reach from the UK without flying. By train, you take the Eurostar to Brussels and change for a fast German or Eurostar train to Cologne, and the best connections take around five hours from London. Our guide to [Christmas markets by train from London](/blog/christmas-markets-by-train-from-london) has the details.

If you'd rather fly, Cologne Bonn airport has direct flights from several UK airports, and Düsseldorf is about 40 minutes away by train. Routes change by season, so check what flies from your nearest airport.

Tip: stay within walking distance of the cathedral or the Old Town. You'll be out until 9 or 10pm most nights, and it's much easier to walk back than to wait for a tram in the cold. December weekends sell out early, so book soon, and think about arriving on a Thursday for a quieter first evening.

sections.heading: Cologne or somewhere else?
sections.text:
Cologne suits you if you want lots of markets in one place, an easy trip by train and a lively city atmosphere. If you'd rather have one very pretty market in a small town, look at [Colmar](/destinations/colmar) or [Strasbourg](/destinations/strasbourg), and for the most traditional German market, [Nuremberg](/destinations/nuremberg).

Our round-up of the [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe) compares the main cities and their 2026 dates, and the [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page has ideas for snow and winter sun too. If you can't agree where to go, add a few ideas to [somewhere.party](/) and let the draw pick.

faqs.question: When do the Cologne Christmas markets open in 2026?
faqs.answer: The harbour market opens first, on 13 November 2026. The cathedral market, the angels' market and Nikolausdorf open on 16 November, and the Old Town market on 23 November.

faqs.question: When do the Cologne Christmas markets close?
faqs.answer: Most close on 23 December 2026. The harbour market stays open until 3 January 2027, and the Old Town market usually runs into early January too.

faqs.question: Are the Cologne Christmas markets open on 22 November 2026?
faqs.answer: Most city-centre markets are closed on Sunday 22 November, a German day of remembrance, and the Old Town market opens the day after.

faqs.question: How many days do you need for the Cologne Christmas markets?
faqs.answer: Two nights is enough to see all the main markets in the evenings and the cathedral, the Rhine and the Chocolate Museum by day.

faqs.question: Can you get to Cologne by train from London?
faqs.answer: Yes. You take the Eurostar to Brussels and change there for Cologne, and the fastest connections take around five hours.
